newsitem.title: BELARUS: Lukashenko refuses Russian invitation to Smolensk.
newsitem.headline: Lukashenko refuses Russian invitation to Smolensk.

text.p: Belarus President Alexander Lukashenko, rebuffing pressure from Moscow to compromise with his opponents, refused on Wednesday to attend peace talks in the Russian town of Smolensk aimed at defusing his country's political crisis.

"The president has decided not to go to Smolensk. He has an extremely tight schedule and so he has decided not to go," Mikhail Podgainy, head of information at the presidential administration, told Reuters.

Asked if Lukashenko's decision not to attend the meeting was linked to the fact that his main political opponent, Semyon Sharetsky who heads the parliament, would be there, Podgainy said: "No. The president is very busy."
Lukashenko's closest aide, Vladimir Zametalin, said the president would not be going because Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, expected to attend, would not be there.
Belarussian state television said the two men agreed that they should meet in the near future and that a solution should be found in line with the present constitution and laws.
Interfax news agency quoted Lukashenko as telling deputies loyal to him that his controversial referendum on Sunday would not be called off, saying "There can be no talk of dropping it."
